title: Spatially Resolved Gene Expression Prediction from H&E Histology Images via Bi-modal Contrastive Learning
authors: Ronald Xie; Kuan Pang; Sai W. Chung; Catia T. Perciani; Sonya A. MacParland; Bo Wang; Gary D. Bader
is_preprint: no (published at NeurIPS 2023; preprint and proceedings both opened)
summary: BLEEP trains image and expression encoders into one embedding with a contrastive loss and predicts a query patch from the nearest reference spots' expression. It is tested on one human liver Visium dataset against ST-Net and HisToGene, shows resilience to experimental artefacts, and does not address privacy or multi-site reference sets.
verified_from: arXiv abs page 2306.01859; NeurIPS proceedings page
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Seed. Reference set is the expression profiles themselves, so route C4 would store those with embeddings.

title: Exemplar Guided Deep Neural Network for Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis of Gene Expression Prediction
authors: Yan Yang; Md Zakir Hossain; Eric A Stone; Shafin Rahman
venue: arXiv preprint (WACV 2023 per authors, not confirmed from a proceedings page)
summary: EGN predicts expression for a slide window by retrieving similar exemplar windows from training slides and feeding them to the regressor. The abstract reports gains over earlier ST-Net-type models on public datasets.
note: Retrieval inside a regression network; venue not verified.

title: Multimodal contrastive learning for spatial gene expression prediction using histology images
authors: Wenwen Min; Zhiceng Shi; Jun Zhang; Jun Wan; Changmiao Wang
summary: mclSTExp learns a joint image and spot-expression embedding that also encodes spot position, in the family of BLEEP. Its results section (seen on the journal page) reports higher correlation than BLEEP on its test slices.
note: Journal page read via web search snippet; abstract via Europe PMC.

title: A visual–omics foundation model to bridge histopathology with spatial transcriptomics
authors: Weiqing Chen; Pengzhi Zhang; Tu N Tran; Yiwei Xiao; Shengyu Li; Vrutant V. Shah; Hao Cheng; Kristopher W. Brannan; Keith Youker; Li Lai; Longhou Fang; Yu Yang; Nhat-Tu Le; Jun-ichi Abe; Shu-Hsia Chen; et al.
summary: OmiCLIP links H&E tissue patches to transcriptomics in a contrastive vision-omics model trained on a large pooled collection of public spatial data. It illustrates central scaling of public data combined with a joint embedding.
note: Abstract read only; number of patches and tasks not extracted.

title: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Cross-Modal Learning for Histology and Gene Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Rushin H. Gindra; Giovanni Palla; Mathias Nguyen; Sophia J. Wagner; Manuel Tran; Fabian J Theis; Dieter Saur; Lorin Crawford; Tingying Peng
summary: HESCAPE builds a pan-organ Xenium benchmark (6 gene panels, 54 donors) to compare image and expression encoders for contrastive pretraining. Contrastive alignment helped mutation classification but lowered direct expression prediction relative to encoders trained without it, and the authors name batch effects as an interfering factor; downstream folds are patient-level.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Seed. Panels mix organs and collection sites, relevant to Q9 on lab/study confounding.

title: VOICE: A Vision-Omics Foundation Model Integrating Direct and Retrieval-Based Prediction of In-situ Single-Cell Gene Expression
authors: Xin Luo; Yicheng Tao; Haoxuan Zeng; Suyuan Wang; Chenzi Ouyang; Meiqi Zhu; Kai Liu; Shuibing Chen; Jie Liu
summary: VOICE fuses a direct regression branch with retrieval of reference cells in a contrastive image-expression space, using a per-gene gate. Trained on 75 Xenium slides (23.2 M cells) it beat a 24-slide version on every metric (+0.013 to +0.047; breast S50 PCC 0.712 to 0.758) and beat the other methods on unseen slides; fusion raised macro PCC 0.3810 to 0.3904 in the 24-slide model.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Two-point data-scale comparison (24 vs 75 slides, Xenium single-cell, not centers); metric is per-gene PCC across all cells of a slide, so slide offsets are NOT removed. Not in the oversight scan.

title: Towards Spatial Transcriptomics-driven Pathology Foundation Models
authors: Konstantin Hemker; Andrew H. Song; Cristina Almagro-Pérez; Guillaume Jaume; Sophia J. Wagner; Anurag Vaidya; Nikola Simidjievski; Mateja Jamnik; Faisal Mahmood
summary: SEAL fine-tunes pathology foundation models in a parameter-efficient way with 700,000+ paired spot-region examples from 14 organs. On HEST-Bench all five encoders improved, the best by 1.33% average PCC, and the authors attribute the small gain to distribution shift from their training data.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Evaluation head is PCA(256) plus ridge, same as the HEST-Bench head. Not in the oversight scan.

title: STPath: a generative foundation model for integrating spatial transcriptomics and whole-slide images
authors: Tinglin Huang; Tianyu Liu; Mehrtash Babadi; Rex Ying; Wengong Jin
summary: STPath is a generative model pretrained on pooled public whole-slide images paired with spatial transcriptomics, predicting many genes across organs without per-dataset fine-tuning. It is the central-scaling alternative; the abstract read here gives no learning curve in training sites or patients.
verified_from: Crossref; EPMC abstract; web search snippet of the Nature page
note: Seed. Pretrained on HEST-1k-type pooled data.

title: Scalable Generation of Spatial Transcriptomics from Histology Images via Whole-Slide Flow Matching
authors: Tinglin Huang; Tianyu Liu; Mehrtash Babadi; Wengong Jin; Rex Ying
is_preprint: no (published version and preprint both opened)
summary: STFlow casts expression prediction as flow matching conditioned on pathology foundation model features and uses spot interactions. It is evaluated on HEST-1k and STimage-1K4M (17 datasets) with an 18% average relative gain over the foundation models.
note: Seed. PDF saved; only the abstract and introduction passage read.

title: Dual-Path Knowledge-Augmented Contrastive Alignment Network for Spatially Resolved Transcriptomics
authors: Wei Zhang; Jiajun Chu; Xinci Liu; Chen Tong; Xinyue Li
summary: DKAN adds gene semantics from an external gene database to a contrastive image-expression alignment network. It is an example of adding text knowledge to the joint-embedding route.
note: Found through a web search result; abstract only.

title: HECLIP: histology-enhanced contrastive learning for imputation of transcriptomics profiles
authors: Qing Wang; Wen-jie Chen; Jing Su; Guangyu Wang; Qianqian Song
summary: HECLIP uses histology-enhanced contrastive learning to impute transcriptomic profiles. It belongs to the BLEEP family of joint-embedding methods.
note: Abstract only.

title: GR2ST: spatial transcriptomics prediction based on graph-enhanced multimodal contrastive learning
authors: Jingli Zhou; Siyuan Li; Rui Han; Xuan Wang; Yadong Wang; Junyi Li
summary: GR2ST combines a graph-enhanced multimodal contrastive objective with a large pathology model to predict spot expression. A further member of the joint-embedding family.
note: Abstract only.

title: MINT: Molecularly Informed Training with Spatial Transcriptomics Supervision for Pathology Foundation Models
authors: Minsoo Lee; Jonghyun Kim; Juseung Yun; Sunwoo Yu; Jongseong Jang
summary: MINT fine-tunes pretrained pathology vision transformers with spatial transcriptomics supervision. It is a further example of adapting the encoder using expression data.
note: Abstract only.

title: Teaching pathology foundation models to accurately predict gene expression with parameter efficient knowledge transfer
authors: Shi Pan; Jianan Chen; Maria Secrier
venue: arXiv preprint; MICCAI 2025 per the papers.miccai.org PDF returned by web search (proceedings page not opened)
summary: PEKA adapts a pathology foundation model with block-affine parameter-efficient tuning plus distillation from a single-cell foundation model. On 206,123 HEST tiles it reports at least a 5% gain over baseline encoders with the HEST PCA-ridge head.
note: PDF saved; abstract and setup passage read.

title: Robustifying pathology foundation models via fine-tuning
authors: Alexandre Filiot; Oskar Thaeter; Benoit Schmauch; Lionel Guillou
summary: A fine-tuning recipe for ten pathology foundation models, aimed at robustness to scanner and staining differences, is tested on PathoROB and on the HEST gene-expression benchmark (ridge on PCA 256). Mean HEST Pearson rose from 0.398 to 0.411 with 9 of 10 models improving; the best models reach 0.4290.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Not in the oversight scan. Encoder adaptation is on pooled public data.

title: Meta-encoder: a unified integration framework for multiple pathological foundation models in cancer detection
authors: Ruitian Gao; Zhaochang Yang; Xin Yuan; Yifan Wang; Yujia Xia; Yufei Zhang; Bingyan Zheng; Yuqiao Gong; Yiping Yue; Yansong Tu; Zhangsheng Yu
summary: Meta-Encoder integrates several pathology foundation models into one encoder for downstream fine-tuning, and its abstract motivates this by the lack of data sharing that makes pooled retraining infeasible. It touches gene-expression prediction among its tasks.
note: Abstract only; possible T-other (federated) relevance flagged for the lead.

title: Benchmarking foundation models as feature extractors for weakly supervised computational pathology
authors: Peter Neidlinger; Omar S. M. El Nahhas; Hannah Sophie Muti; Tim Lenz; Michael Hoffmeister; Hermann Brenner; Marko van Treeck; Rupert Langer; Bastian Dislich; Hans Michael Behrens; Christoph Röcken; Sebastian Foersch; Daniel Truhn; Antonio Marra; Oliver Lester Saldanha; et al.
summary: Benchmarks 19 pathology foundation models on 13 external cohorts (6,818 patients) with weakly supervised tasks, to compare encoders on external data. It supports the choice of encoder as a lever; its tasks are biomarkers rather than spatial expression.
note: Found by title lookup, not by a query.

title: HEST-1k: A Dataset for Spatial Transcriptomics and Histology Image Analysis
authors: Guillaume Jaume; Paul Doucet; Andrew H. Song; Ming Y. Lu; Cristina Almagro-Pérez; Sophia J. Wagner; Anurag J. Vaidya; Richard J. Chen; Drew F. K. Williamson; Ahrong Kim; Faisal Mahmood
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks (proceedings page https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/60a899cc31f763be0bde781a75e04458-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks_Track.html); arXiv preprint
is_preprint: no (published version and preprint both opened)
summary: HEST-1k pools public spatial transcriptomics and H&E data and defines HEST-Benchmark with patient-stratified folds and a PCA-ridge head. Across 11 encoders, benchmark Pearson rises with encoder size on a logarithmic trend (R = 0.81, p < 0.01), a model-size scaling result; the sections read give no learning curve in training patients or sites.
verified_from: arXiv abs page 2406.16192; NeurIPS proceedings page
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Seed.

title: Benchmarking the translational potential of spatial gene expression prediction from histology
authors: Chuhan Wang; Adam S. Chan; Xiaohang Fu; Shila Ghazanfar; Jinman Kim; Ellis Patrick; Jean Y. H. Yang
summary: Benchmark of eleven histology-to-expression methods on five spatial datasets, validated externally on TCGA, scored on 28 metrics over accuracy, generalisability, translational potential, usability and efficiency; no method led everywhere. The authors note that PCC and SSIM were low across methods on HER2+ ST data.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Seed (oversight scan describes it as weak transfer across studies; the passages read give the cross-study design, not a verified numeric weak-transfer figure).

title: Performance of deep learning methods for spatial gene expression prediction from histology images: a comprehensive assessment
authors: Jacky Xie; Xiao Tan; Yuanhao Jiang; Hao Nguyen; Nan Ye; Quan Nguyen
summary: Assessment of deep learning methods for expression prediction from histology; its results snippet places DeepSpaCE, STimage, BLEEP and DeepPT above Hist2ST, HisToGene and ST-Net in-distribution. It has a generalization section for out-of-distribution data.
verified_from: Crossref; EPMC abstract; web search snippet
note: Abstract and snippet only; out-of-distribution section not read.

title: From histology to spatial transcriptomics: establishing a lightweight single-patch baseline
authors: Hyungyum Jang; Hyunsoo Shin; Hawon Lee; Yena Jang; Sung Hoon Jung; Minji Jeon
summary: Establishes the accuracy attainable from single isolated patches as a baseline against methods that use whole-slide spatial context. Relevant as a lightweight comparator for any head.
note: Abstract only.

title: The impact of site-specific digital histology signatures on deep learning model accuracy and bias
authors: Frederick M. Howard; James Dolezal; Sara Kochanny; Jefree Schulte; Heather Chen; Lara Heij; Dezheng Huo; Rita Nanda; Olufunmilayo I. Olopade; Jakob N. Kather; Nicole Cipriani; Robert L. Grossman; Alexander T. Pearson
summary: Shows in TCGA (over 3,000 patients, six cancers) that tissue-source-site signatures are detectable by deep learning despite colour normalisation. Standard cross-validation made outcomes including gene expression look predictable and inflated accuracy; the authors propose a quadratic-programming split so training and validation never share a site.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2020.12.03.410845 is the earlier version. Direct support for leave-one-site-out in TCGA.

title: Do Histopathological Foundation Models Eliminate Batch Effects? A Comparative Study
authors: Jonah Kömen; Hannah Marienwald; Jonas Dippel; Julius Hense
summary: Tests whether histopathology foundation models remove site batch effects on five TCGA-LUSC sites and CAMELYON16 and finds that site signatures remain in feature space, with stain normalisation of limited help. It cautions that models on top of such features may fail to generalise across sites.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end.

title: Towards robust foundation models for digital pathology
authors: Jonah Kömen; Edwin D. de Jong; Julius Hense; Hannah Marienwald; Jonas Dippel; Philip Naumann; Eric Marcus; Lukas Ruff; Maximilian Alber; Jonas Teuwen; Frederick Klauschen; Klaus-Robert Müller
summary: PathoROB benchmarks 20 pathology foundation models on four multi-center datasets (28 classes, 34 centers) with a robustness index and finds all encode center signatures to some degree. Stain normalisation and batch correction in representation space reduce but do not remove the problem.
verified_from: Crossref; EPMC abstract; web search of PMC page
note: Preprint arXiv:2507.17845 (Kömen et al.) opened as an abs page; same work. Abstract level only.

title: Deep feature batch correction using ComBat for machine learning applications in computational pathology.
authors: Pierre Murchan; Pilib Ó Broin; Anne-Marie Baird; Orla Sheils; Stephen P Finn
summary: Applies ComBat to deep features of TCGA colon and stomach slides to reduce site-specific confounding in machine-learning models. It is a feature-space method for site effects that could be applied per center.
note: Abstract only.

title: STimage-1K4M: A histopathology image-gene expression dataset for spatial transcriptomics
authors: Jiawen Chen; Muqing Zhou; Wenrong Wu; Jinwei Zhang; Yun Li; Didong Li
venue: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks (per the GitHub citation in a search result); arXiv preprint
summary: STimage-1K4M gathers 1,149 slides and about 4.3 M image-expression pairs from Spatial Transcriptomics, Visium and VisiumHD, human and mouse, 50 tissues. It is a second public pool beside HEST-1k for simulating centers.

title: SpaRED benchmark: Enhancing Gene Expression Prediction from Histology Images with Spatial Transcriptomics Completion
authors: Gabriel Mejia; Daniela Ruiz; Paula Cárdenas; Leonardo Manrique; Daniela Vega; Pablo Arbeláez
summary: SpaRED collects 26 standardised Visium datasets and defines intra- and inter-patient generalisation tasks. A further public source for center simulation.
note: Abstract only.

title: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory
authors: Mirac Suzgun; Mert Yuksekgonul; Federico Bianchi; Dan Jurafsky; James Zou
summary: Dynamic Cheatsheet gives a language model an evolving memory of strategies and solutions at test time without weight updates. Reported gains are in reasoning tasks (for example AIME 2020-2024 from 6.7% to 40.6% for Claude 3.5 Sonnet), not numeric regression.
note: Retrieved PDF; targeted passages (methods, results, limitations) read, not end to end. Closest published relative of round 6's cheatsheets; no tabular or omics tasks.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
authors: Qizheng Zhang; Changran Hu; Shubhangi Upasani; Boyuan Ma; Fenglu Hong; Vamsidhar Kamanuru; Jay Rainton; Chen Wu; Mengmeng Ji; Hanchen Li; Urmish Thakker; James Zou; Kunle Olukotun
summary: ACE treats the model context as an evolving playbook updated by generation, reflection and curation, to avoid brevity bias and context collapse. Its tasks are agent and domain-reasoning benchmarks.
note: PDF saved, not read beyond abstract.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
authors: Andrew Zhao; Daniel Huang; Quentin Xu; Matthieu Lin; Yong-Jin Liu; Gao Huang
venue: arXiv preprint (AAAI 2024 per authors, not confirmed)
summary: ExpeL lets an LLM agent gather experiences and extract natural-language insights across tasks, then use them at inference without fine-tuning. Evaluated on decision-making tasks.
note: PDF saved, abstract level only.

title: From Words to Numbers: Your Large Language Model Is Secretly A Capable Regressor When Given In-Context Examples
authors: Robert Vacareanu; Vlad-Andrei Negru; Vasile Suciu; Mihai Surdeanu
summary: Shows that large language models given examples in context can perform linear and non-linear regression comparable to Random Forest or gradient boosting on synthetic tasks. It is the closest evidence that a model with labelled spots in its prompt can act as a regressor.
note: Abstract only.

title: TabLLM: Few-shot Classification of Tabular Data with Large Language Models
authors: Stefan Hegselmann; Alejandro Buendia; Hunter Lang; Monica Agrawal; Xiaoyi Jiang; David Sontag
venue: arXiv preprint (AISTATS 2023 per authors, not confirmed)
summary: TabLLM serialises tabular rows into text and prompts a language model for zero- and few-shot classification, with a fine-tuned few-shot variant. It is competitive in the few-shot regime on tabular benchmarks.
note: Abstract only.

title: LLM Processes: Numerical Predictive Distributions Conditioned on Natural Language
authors: James Requeima; John Bronskill; Dami Choi; Richard E. Turner; David Duvenaud
summary: LLM Processes elicit numerical predictive distributions from language models conditioned on natural-language prior knowledge. It tests the idea of injecting text knowledge into a regression model.
note: Found by T7-q11 on arXiv; abstract only.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Patrick Lewis; Ethan Perez; Aleksandra Piktus; Fabio Petroni; Vladimir Karpukhin; Naman Goyal; Heinrich Küttler; Mike Lewis; Wen-tau Yih; Tim Rocktäschel; Sebastian Riedel; Douwe Kiela
venue: NeurIPS 2020 (not confirmed from a proceedings page); arXiv preprint

note: Abstract only; included as primary reference of the term.

title: Simple and effective embedding model for single-cell biology built from ChatGPT
authors: Yiqun Chen; James Zou
summary: GenePT builds gene embeddings from GPT-3.5 text of gene descriptions and cell embeddings by expression-weighted averaging. It is evidence for the textual knowledge-base route in single-cell data.
note: Found by title lookup. Crossref gives year 2024; EPMC lists 2025.

title: Learning Relative Gene Expression Trends from Pathology Images in Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Kazuya Nishimura; Haruka Hirose; Ryoma Bise; Kaito Shiku; Yasuhiro Kojima
summary: Proposes STRank, a loss that learns relative expression patterns instead of absolute levels, on the assumption that relative patterns stay consistent across experiments while absolute values carry batch effects and noise. Tested on synthetic and real data; bears on the choice of a metric that removes slide-level offsets.
note: Abstract only; found by scanning the NeurIPS 2025 title index (q01/q02/q08).

title: SToFM: a Multi-scale Foundation Model for Spatial Transcriptomics
authors: Suyuan Zhao; Yizhen Luo; Ganbo Yang; Yan Zhong; Hao Zhou; Zaiqing Nie
summary: A foundation model for spatial transcriptomics that extracts multi-scale information from tissue slices. It is ST-side pretraining on pooled data, an alternative to histology-side encoder adaptation.

title: STHELAR, a multi-tissue dataset linking spatial transcriptomics and histology for cell type annotation
authors: Félicie Giraud-Sauveur; Quentin Blampey; Hakim Benkirane; Arianna Marinello; Paul-Henry Cournède; Stergios Christodoulidis
summary: STHELAR links 31 human Xenium FFPE sections from 22 cancer and 9 non-cancer patients (16 tissues, over 11 million cells) to H&E images with cell-type labels. It is a further public Xenium source whose panels and sites could define simulated centers.

title: ST-ConMa: a multimodal foundation framework for spatial transcriptomics via image–gene contrastive and matching learning
authors: Taelim Yeom; Dongha Choi; Hyunju Lee
summary: ST-ConMa is a multimodal foundation framework for spatial transcriptomics with image-gene contrastive and matching objectives, aimed at generalisation across platforms. Another member of the joint-embedding family.
note: Abstract only.

title: Slide Selection Introduces Sampling-Induced Prediction Uncertainty in Digital Pathology AI: Evidence from Multi-Slide Breast Cancer Cohorts
authors: Onur C. Koyun; Yongxin Guo; Hao Lu; Muhammet Fatih Demir; Abbas Alili; Nabil Rahoui; Diana Cardona; Metin N. Gurcan
summary: Quantifies how choosing which slide represents a patient changes MIL predictions of molecular phenotypes, training in TCGA-BRCA (1,006 patients) and testing in CPTAC-BRCA (122 patients), and evaluates multi-slide aggregation. It documents slide-to-slide variability that bears on a metric computed within slides.
note: Abstract only; bulk-level labels, not spatial expression.
